question: Your team runs Claude Code in CI with the -p flag to label new bug reports with a component and a severity. Labels with high field-level confidence are applied without human review. Each week, reviewers check a uniform random 2% sample of these high-confidence labels, and the measured error rate stays low. Developers then find that labels for the small mobile component have shown a new error pattern for weeks. How should the team change its weekly audit?

options.text: Draw the weekly random sample separately within each component and field, so small components get enough reviewed labels to show their own error rate.
options.reason: The guide recommends stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions for ongoing error rate measurement and novel pattern detection. Stratifying ensures that a small segment, such as the mobile component, is sampled often enough to reveal its errors.

options.text: Keep the uniform sample, and report one combined error rate for all components and fields to the team each week.
options.reason: The guide warns that aggregate accuracy metrics can mask poor performance on specific segments or fields. One combined rate is exactly what hid the mobile errors.

options.text: Replace the weekly sample with a one-time check of the mobile component's labels against a labeled validation set, and then return to the uniform weekly sample.
options.reason: A one-time check gives no ongoing error rate measurement. After it, the uniform sample again under-samples small components, so the next novel error pattern can go unnoticed, against the guide's stratified sampling practice.

options.text: Raise the confidence threshold for automatic labeling, and keep the same uniform 2% weekly sample of all high-confidence labels.
options.reason: A higher threshold does not change how the audit samples. The uniform sample still contains very few mobile labels, so new error patterns in small segments stay hidden, which stratified sampling is meant to prevent.
